title: 2019 AMC 10A Problem 12
statement: Melanie computes the mean \(\mu,\) the median \(M,\) and the modes of the \(365\) values that are the dates in the months of \(2019.\) Thus her data consist of \(12\) copies of \(1,\) \(12\) copies of \(2,\) and so on through \(12\) copies of \(28,\) then \(11\) copies of \(29,\) \(11\) copies of \(30,\) and \(7\) copies of \(31.\) Let \(d\) be the median of the modes. Which of the following statements is true?

solutions.text:
The modes are all the integers from \(1\) through \(28,\) so their median is \(d=\dfrac{14+15}{2}=14.5.\)

There are \(365\) entries, so \(M\) is the \(183\)rd number. The dates from \(1\) through \(15\) occupy \(15 \cdot 12 = 180\) positions, so \(M=16.\)

The sum of all dates is \[\begin{aligned}12(1+\cdots+28)&+11(29+30)\\&+7\cdot31=5738.\end{aligned}\] Hence \(\mu=\dfrac{5738}{365}\approx15.72.\)

Therefore \[ d \lt \mu \lt M. \] Thus, E is the correct answer.
hints: Understand which dates appear \(12\) times and which appear fewer times
Compare the mean, median, and modes from the calendar counts
